key_insight: Long-term yields in three short-rate models can be computed as ground-state energies using VQE, with a single-setting estimator sharply reducing hardware error.
engineering_relevance: Mapping bond-pricing equations to quantum Hamiltonians enables a hardware-tested workflow for financial models, including Black–Karasinski, which lacks a closed-form solution.
method: Transform Feynman–Kac pricing equations into Schrödinger ground-state problems.
Exploit positive stoquastic ground states to estimate energy from computational-basis samples in one measurement setting.
Combine WKB-guided bit-flip deconvolution, readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation.
evidence_signal: On ibm_cleveland, four-qubit estimates were within 33–125 bp of grid ground-state energies versus 791–1,129 bp for Pauli-measurement VQE; IonQ Forte Enterprise showed proportional error reductions.
watch_item: Four-qubit results and an in-sample Treasury correlation do not establish scalability or out-of-sample financial accuracy.
paper_title: Long-term yields of short-rate models as Feynman-Kac ground states: a variational quantum eigensolver with single-setting energy estimation on two NISQ platforms
